chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Mavouzy starts his own band and it collapses
summary: Mavouzy's rival band on the Grand Boulevard drew people on opening day, but a Jamaican trumpeter cut him with a razor and the audience returned to Butler's.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Then we liked to gamble. So people would wait for Mavouzy and give him some of that punch. They'd give him some punch. And Mavouzy would get that punch and go out (inaudible) and get him again. (Inaudible). Then he was so jealous, everytime I talked to a lady, (inaudible).

salary before them other cats would get it. So he ended up he'd get his/ "You'd better leave Jacques alone. Jacques is old Renard, he's an old fox, he's making fun of you. I said, I love you Mavouzy (inaudible). Latin people. You've got to tell him now and then you love him. If you don't tell him you love him (inaudible).
All right, Mavouzy got mad, said he's going to make a band of his own. So he got (all of the) Charlie Parker and

had a band on the Grand Boulevard. Well, the first night, as I told you, (inaudible) he wanted to have all the money and all the women, everything. He and the trumpet player, a boy from Jamaica, good trumpet player, too, very good trumpet player, well, something happened --

No, (inaudible) directly from Jamaica. And it seemed as though something happened and they got to arguing or something and the boy, as I told you, pulled out his razor and started working on Mavouzy, on his backside (inaudible).

So now, they were supposed to run me out of Paris. So I kept laying on "Night Train". And so he sends scouts out to see what's happening. Well, that afternoon, everybody was over there to hear Mavouzy. That night, half of them was back. The next day, everybody was back. Wasn't nothing but Mavouzy and all his buddies over there. So they was over there fighting (inaudible) and the man had to close.
And then, well, you know after that. We was making it. We were cooking. So ________ asked me to start up. Now, that was during the war.
